newsitem.title: UK: New British premier in Northern Ireland visit.
newsitem.headline: New British premier in Northern Ireland visit.

text.p: Britain's new Prime Minister Tony Blair arrived in troubled Northern Ireland on Friday to underline his Labour government's commitment to seek an end to 28 years of sectarian and political conflict.
Blair's one-day visit, his first outside London since he came to power in May 1 elections, took place against a backdrop of continued violence which has killed three people in 10 days.
His first stop was the southern city of Armagh. The rest of his itinerary was not disclosed for security reasons.
Tight security was enforced around Armagh. Army helicopters flew overhead and armed police and troops were in position around the city, witnesses said.

Protestant Loyalists fighting to maintain British rule of the province have killed two Roman Catholics in the past 10 days in apparent retaliation for attacks by Irish republicans who want the province reunited with Ireland.
The shadowy Irish National Liberation Army (INLA) killed an off-duty policeman in a Belfast bar this month.
The main republican group, the Irish Republican Army (IRA), has been at war with Britain since it ended a 17-month ceasefire in February, 1996.
The return to violence has led to the IRA's political wing Sinn Fein being excluded from peace talks.
